payload.reason: One proposal (practice), selected as the core. It was checked against the survey, the investigation and five spikes, and one seam was changed: the counter correction is keyed on the child's successful keep-open, because spike 1 measured that a rule keyed on attempted opens under-counts. The report was only a title. This design assumes the slice must (1) commit a measured verdict for each of the three tests, (2) make `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx` green under the engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, and (3) keep any last-access side effect visible in the routine suite. These are the build check's three derived criteria. The acceptance command is the engine's bug project exiting 0.
payload.selection_rationale:
Each piece was chosen against what was measured, not against taste.

1. The verdict is 'both', and the evidence is measured. All three red tests are an environment fault. The engine's TEMP is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, where a write-class open of a child moves the parent's last access, and the fixtures back-date each parent before its children:
   - 20/23 pass vs 23/23.
   - 689/692 pass vs 692/692.
   - DisableLastAccess=2 is ENABLED in both locations, so that setting is not the cause.
   Underneath the fault is one real defect in this project. The scanner's own keep-open of each child folder moves the parent there, yet LastAccessKept still counts the parent as kept: (7,7) against 4 unmoved, in 5 of 5 trees.

2. Product fix: the counter only. Spike 1 rejected the attempted-open rule (tree d: kept 0, truth 1). Its step 6 showed that a refused child open does not move the parent, so the rule is keyed on the child's successful keep-open. The plain-open alternative was never run. It was predicted to move about 6 of 7 folders and to give up the children's own kept times, so it was not chosen. The counters are internal (Q-103, Q-159), so making them true is the whole product fix.

3. TempTree redirect: from spike 4 (conditional). Under the engine's TEMP it measured 23/23 three times and 692/692, with nothing created under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests. Its constraints are honoured: the opt-in cloud rigs are not redirected, and this design says so. The engine-side fix (spike 5, a go) lives in taad_v3's launch.py, outside this repository, and would leave any other launcher red. It is filed for the person, not built.

4. Deepest-first back-dating: from spike 2. It was a no-go as the only fix, but it is kept because it moves any future failure in luafv's location from a precondition that hides the cause to the scan assertion that names it. That shift was measured: :68/:96 became :78/:87.

5. New Facts: spike 3 was the go. With the correction it reported kept 4 of 7, and without it the Fact failed 3 of 3 (7 vs 4). The Facts are the only thing that keeps the side effect in front of the routine suite once the redirect exists.

The practice designer raised its own over_engineering_flag, and that is honoured. Not built:
   - a read-back pass after the walk;
   - luafv detection in Core;
   - a KnownWorkarounds entry for an internal counter;
   - a set of every kept folder;
   - edits to the engine.

The one addition over the proposal is a pure TempTree root-choice function. It gives the redirect's four branches a machine check without changing the process environment.

components.name: Scanner kept-counter correction
components.responsibility:
CountListingOpen (Scanner.cs:311-318) gains the folder's path, and both callers pass it: ListRoot (:235, win32Root) and the walk (:182-193).

When io.KeptLastAccess is true:
1. _lastAccessKept++ as today.
2. If the folder is at or under %SystemRoot%, add its path to a per-scan HashSet<string>(OrdinalIgnoreCase), trimmed of trailing separators. The location test reuses Scanner's existing IsAtOrUnder, the sync-root test used by KeepsLastAccess, against Environment.GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows) computed once per scan.
3. Derive the parent with plain string operations: trim trailing separators, then cut at the last separator. This keeps the form CountListingOpen received.
4. If set.Remove(parent) succeeds, _lastAccessKept--.

Removing from the set is what makes each parent come out at most once.

The correction fires only on a child whose keep-open SUCCEEDED, never on an attempted or refused one.

What does not change:
- no new opens and no change to any access mask;
- no change to which folders are asked;
- no change to SynchronousIoCancel.

The root's parent lies outside the scan, is never in the set, and is never touched.
components.key_interactions:
Reads SynchronousIoCancel.KeptLastAccess. It is set at Open (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:488-543) and is still readable after DirectoryReader.Read closes the handle, which is how today's counter already works.

Reachable only behind the existing DecideLastAccess/KeepsLastAccess gates: local NTFS, not remote, not cloud, not a sync root. The InsideExcludedStore branch stays uncounted and opens nothing.

Runs on the single scan thread, where a parent is counted before any of its children is opened (SL-042). ProbePass and SizeProbe file opens are read-class and were measured not to move anything (plain\sub and links\b-second never moved).

components.name: LastAccessKept contract text
components.responsibility:
Rewrite the doc comment at ScanResult.cs:190-194. It currently assumes that a successful -1 set means the time stayed.

New text: kept = asked folders whose keep-open succeeded, minus folders at or under %SystemRoot% whose last access the scan's own later keep-open of a child folder moved. That move was measured in %SystemRoot%\Temp and is attributed to UAC file virtualization. It is a stated limit of the scan, not something it prevents.

The counters stay internal (Q-103, Q-159), and the App shows nothing.
components.key_interactions: Read by LastAccessTests :85, HeldOpenTreeTests :82-83, the SL-096 bug test :139 and LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.

components.name: TempTree root choice and explicit-root constructor
components.responsibility:
The TestsRoot initialiser (TempTree.cs:17) calls a pure internal static ChooseTestsRoot(string tempPath, string windowsDir, string localAppData), passing GetTempPath(), GetFolderPath(Windows) and GetFolderPath(LocalApplicationData).

Rules:
- If GetFullPath(tempPath) is at or under windowsDir (case-insensitive, separator boundary), the root is localAppData\Temp\fsa-tests.
- Otherwise the root is tempPath\fsa-tests.
- If the redirect target is itself at or under windowsDir (a SYSTEM or service-profile run), it throws with a named cause, the way TempTree already refuses FAT32 and compressed folders.

The NTFS and compression refusals (:25-31) apply to whichever root is chosen.

A new internal TempTree(string testsRoot) constructor lets the Windows-folder Facts reuse PathOf, the SDDL deny helper and Dispose. Dispose clears deny ACEs before deleting with .NET Directory.Delete; PowerShell's Remove-Item is denied in C:\Windows\Temp.
components.key_interactions: Every TempTree-based test, including the counting-rule tests. They stay real NTFS trees and are never skipped. Under a machine TEMP they now sit in the user's own TEMP (the HKCU value, measured as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp), where SL-089 already put the window cases.

components.responsibility:
Spike 2's one-line edit at :235: `foreach (string path in Enumerable.Reverse(Observed).Append(Path.Combine(control, "c.txt")).Append(control))`.

Observed itself keeps its order, so the snapshot pairing is unchanged. If the fixture ever lands where luafv acts, it fails at the metadata diff (:78), not at the 'was not back-dated' preconditions (:68, :96-97).

components.responsibility: Spike 2's one-line edit at :69: `string[] kept = [tree.PathOf("open"), tree.PathOf(@"refusing\sub"), tree.Root];`. Root is back-dated last. The (4,3) assertion at :85 is unchanged.

components.name: LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests
components.responsibility:
Facts in the default suite that are never skipped and carry no excluded Trait. Each builds through new TempTree(Path.Combine(GetFolderPath(Windows), "Temp", "fsa-tests")).

(1) AScanUnderTheWindowsTempFolderCountsAsKeptOnlyTheFoldersThatStayedOld
- A Theory over how the root is spelled: as-is, lower-case, trailing separator.
- Tree: the 7-folder, 4-file nested tree (root, plain, plain\sub, plain\empty, links, links\a-first, links\b-second).
- Back-dated deepest-first to 48 h.
- Precondition: every entry reads at least 47 h old, and any that does not is named.
- Runs the real Scanner.Scan.
- Asserts: Completed; LastAccessAsked == 7; LastAccessKept == the number of tree folders still at least 47 h old.

(2) AChildThatRefusesWriteAttributesLeavesItsParentCountedAsKept
- Tree: R\refusing\x.bin.
- Setup order: deny FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES on `refusing` (no inheritance), then back-date x.bin, then back-date R last.
- `refusing` is exempt from the precondition, because setting the ACE moves its time and the deny stops it being back-dated.
- Asserts: asked 2, and kept == the number of folders still old (predicted 1).

(3) OutsideTheWindowsFolderEveryKeptFolderStaysKept
- Tree (1) under TempTree's default root.
- Asserts kept == asked == unmoved == 7.

Every case asserts its tree is gone after Dispose: this user cannot list C:\Windows\Temp, so a leftover could never be found.

Failure messages give (asked, kept), the folders that moved, and what each direction means:
- over-count: the correction is missing, or the location list is too narrow;
- under-count: the rule is keyed wrongly, or luafv no longer moves parents on this machine.
components.key_interactions: Keeps the real side effect, and the truth of the counters, in the routine `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`. The bug project is outside FsAnalyser.slnx and cannot do this job.

SL-096 acceptance bug test (unchanged)

It stays out of FsAnalyser.slnx: it takes the assembly name FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, which would collide.

components.name: Triage record
components.responsibility:
Records the verdict for each test, with the measured numbers.

(a) APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime: environment only. Parent-first back-dating in luafv's location resets the control. No scan side effect.

(b) TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata: the same environment fault hid a real side effect. Under %SystemRoot%\Temp the scan's child keep-opens move root, plain and links (5 of 5 trees), and the counter over-reported (7,7) against 4 unmoved. That is now fixed in the counter, and stated as a limit of the scan.

(c) AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributesIsListedPlainlyAndCountedInFull: fixture order plus the same side effect. Spike 2 saw Root move during Scans.Run.

Also records:
- ruled out: DisableLastAccess=2 (ENABLED); the kernel-memory lead (Luaf freed 59 of 60).
- not measured: %ProgramData%, %ProgramFiles%, Windows 10, whether luafv itself is the cause (needs an administrator), and the root's own parent.

This is the measured triage Q-190 asks for. Closing that question stays with a person.

key_decisions.decision: Verdict: both. All three red tests are an environment fault: the engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP puts the fixtures where a write-class child open moves the parent's last access, and the fixtures back-date parents first. Beneath that is one real defect of this project: LastAccessKept over-reports in that location. DisableLastAccess=2 is ruled out.

Fix the counter, not the opens. When a child folder's keep-open succeeds (io.KeptLastAccess true), take its parent out of LastAccessKept once, if that parent is at or under %SystemRoot% and was counted kept.
key_decisions.rationale:
Spike 1: the attempted-open rule is a no-go (tree d: kept 0, truth 1). Its step 6 showed a refused child open leaves the parent unmoved.

On tree (b) the successful-open rule equals spike 3's measured patch, which gave kept 4 of 7.

Opening children without write-attributes was never run, and was predicted to move about 6 of 7 folders. The counter is internal (Q-103, Q-159), so making it true is the entire product fix.

key_decisions.decision: The affected location is %SystemRoot% only. It is tested with Scanner's existing IsAtOrUnder against GetFolderPath(Windows), held in one place.
key_decisions.rationale:
Only C:\Windows\Temp was measured. %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles% are recalled from the luafv namespace and not measured, and writing there is the person's step. Widening is one line.

Reusing the sync-root comparison keeps one rule for case and separator boundaries in Scanner, instead of a second path comparison.

key_decisions.decision: Track only kept folders at or under %SystemRoot%, in a per-scan OrdinalIgnoreCase HashSet keyed by the path as CountListingOpen received it, trimmed of trailing separators. Derive the parent with string operations.
key_decisions.rationale:
Spike 1 tracked every kept folder, which on a whole-C: scan (about 920k folders) costs on the order of 100 MB against a 1 GB budget where 731 MiB is already measured.

Under C:\Windows, write-attributes is refused for most folders (Q-103's figure, recalled), so the set stays small.

String-only derivation keeps the parent in exactly the form its own count used. It also avoids depending on whether TheScannerMakesNoBclFileSystemCalls admits System.IO.Path.

key_decisions.decision: Do not try to stop the side effect itself. The scan keeps its opens and masks, and the move is stated as a limit in ScanResult's contract text and the triage record.
key_decisions.rationale:
The parent's own -1 handle is closed before its children are opened, and the -1 suppression covers only operations through that handle (recalled), so nothing in the scanner's current shape can prevent another component's open of the parent from stamping it.

Avoiding the move would need a product-level choice (plain-open children, holding handles), which nobody has measured. Q-159 defers last-access work until file-age features are designed. Filed as later work.

Spike 4: 23/23 three times and 692/692 under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, with 0 directories created under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests. This fix holds whatever launches the suite.

Spike 5's fix lives in taad_v3's launch.py, outside this repo. HKCU TEMP was measured to be %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, so the counting-rule tests still run in the user's own %TEMP%.

Back-dating parents first is a fixture bug wherever luafv acts. Spike 2 measured that, with the reorder, the failures move from the preconditions (:68, :96) to the scan assertions (:78, :87), which name the real cause.

Under user TEMP all 23 still pass, so the reorder does not break the fixtures.

key_decisions.decision: Add never-skipped Facts in Core.Tests that build in %SystemRoot%\Temp on purpose and assert kept == unmoved, not <=.
key_decisions.rationale:
The redirect alone would turn this slice's defect back into silence. Equality catches both directions:
- over-count (the defect; spike 3: 7 vs 4 without the correction, 3 of 3);
- under-count (spike 1's wrong rule: 0 vs 1).

A future write-class open added to the scan would also show up, as kept > unmoved.

They fail loudly, never skip, which is the project's habit for tests on real trees.

key_decisions.decision: No KnownWorkarounds entry and no in-app notice.
The opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT rigs (SyncRootRig/CloudRig use GetTempPath directly) are not redirected. This is recorded as a limit and filed.
key_decisions.rationale: They are outside the three tests and outside the default filter, and nobody has measured them with a redirect. Spike 4's constraint allows keeping them opt-in as long as that is said.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement, and the reviewer is the first to argue with it.

Each seam was checked against the measurements instead:

1. Spike 3's 'go' ran experiment 1's patch, which is the attempted-open rule spike 1 measured under-counting on tree (d). This design keys on the child's successful keep-open instead. On tree (b) every child keep-open succeeds, so the two rules are identical and spike 3's kept 4 of 7 and 693/693 carry over. On tree (d) only the prediction exists (kept 1 == truth 1). It is a material case owed to build, not a claim.

2. Redirect vs criterion 3. The TempTree redirect alone would hide the side effect from the routine suite. It is kept only paired with never-skipped Facts that build in %SystemRoot%\Temp on purpose. Architecture rule 1 keeps them from being skipped or traited out.

3. Reorder vs redirect. Deepest-first back-dating acts only where the redirect does not reach. They do not interact.

4. Two assertion strengths. The bug test asserts kept <= unmoved and the new Facts assert kept == unmoved. With the correction both hold (4 == 4), and nothing contradicts.

5. Contract vs decided questions. The ScanResult text changes meaning, but the counters stay internal (Q-103, Q-159). So there is no KnownWorkarounds entry and no notice, and Q-186's workaround list is untouched.

6. Spike 4's constraints:
   - the cloud rigs stay unredirected, and that is said and filed;
   - the shared %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests is separated by per-tree GUID folders;
   - its 4 stale directories are left alone.

7. What was redesigned at the seams:
   - the Scanner's location test reuses the existing sync-root IsAtOrUnder, not a second comparison with its own case and boundary rules;
   - the parent is derived by string from the form CountListingOpen received, normalised for a trailing separator. This is tested by the trailing-separator spelling case;
   - ChooseTestsRoot takes its inputs, so its branches have a machine check.

Architecture rules: two, both over tests. The production change is a few lines inside Scanner and constrains nothing about which project may depend on which.

Rule 2's patterns have not been run against the existing Core.Tests files. If one fires on a test that only uses 'C:\Windows\Temp' as a sample string and builds nothing there, that file goes into except_files at build. The rule is not to be deleted.

architecture_rules.name: the Windows-folder last-access tests are never skipped or filtered out of the default suite
architecture_rules.because: Once TempTree redirects out of %SystemRoot%, these are the only default-suite tests that run where the scan's side effect exists. Skipping them, or tagging them with a Trait the default VSTestTestCaseFilter excludes, puts the over-reporting counter back into silence. That is the 'regression hides in the noise' this slice exists to end.

architecture_rules.name: no Core test builds a fixture in %SystemRoot%\Temp except the deliberate one
architecture_rules.because: In %SystemRoot%\Temp a folder's last access moves whenever one of its children is opened with a write-class access, so a fixture placed there passes or fails on that driver behaviour rather than on what it tests. That is how the three tests went red unnoticed through six validations. Also, this user cannot list that folder, so a tree that a failed cleanup leaves there can be neither found nor removed without an administrator.

contracts.name: ScanResult.LastAccessKept (internal counter)
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user, in-process. Visible only to assemblies granted InternalsVisibleTo (FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, ScanArm).
contracts.error_cases:
No new error paths.
- A refused write-attributes open still falls back to the plain open and counts as asked but not kept, and it never takes a parent out.
- A cancelled scan leaves partial counters, as now.
contracts.notes:
New meaning: asked folders whose keep-open succeeded, minus folders at or under %SystemRoot% that the scan's own later successful keep-open of a child folder moved.

Invariants: 0 <= kept <= asked; no folder is counted twice or taken out twice; outside %SystemRoot% the meaning is exactly as before.

The App never shows it (Q-103, Q-159).

contracts.name: TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot(tempPath, windowsDir, localAppData)
contracts.error_cases: Throws with a named cause when the redirect target is itself at or under windowsDir. The NTFS and compression refusals still apply to the chosen root.
contracts.notes:
- tempPath at or under windowsDir (case-insensitive, separator boundary): localAppData\Temp\fsa-tests.
- Otherwise: tempPath\fsa-tests.

Engine-TEMP and user-TEMP runs share the same folder and are kept apart by per-tree GUID folders.

contracts.name: TempTree(string testsRoot)
contracts.error_cases: The same NTFS and compression refusals as the default constructor. Dispose clears deny ACEs, then deletes with .NET Directory.Delete.

contracts.notes: $env:TEMP=$env:TMP='C:\WINDOWS\TEMP'; pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx must exit 0 with Failed: 0. The same command under the user's TEMP gives the same result. The opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT and Network traits are not covered: they still fail 4/4 under the engine's TEMP (filed).

contracts.name: Mutation check of the Windows-folder Facts
contracts.notes:
In a scratch copy:
- With the correction hunk reverted (touch Scanner.cs before rebuilding), the nested-tree Fact must fail with kept 7 against 4.
- With the rule keyed on attempted rather than successful child opens, the refusing-child Fact must fail with kept 0 against 1.

outside_claims.claim: In C:\Windows\Temp on this PC, opening a child file or folder with a write-class access (FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, WRITE_DATA, DELETE, WRITE_DAC and others) and OPEN_EXISTING moves the parent folder's last-access time to now, synchronously inside the child's CreateFile. Read-class opens do not. In %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp on the same NTFS volume nothing moves.

prior_art.pattern: A last-access test that depends on the environment gets labelled 'Known Build Error' and stays open for years. This is the 'known red' failure this slice avoids by diagnosing and pinning instead.
A Windows last-access test passed or failed depending on the machine's NtfsDisableLastAccessUpdate value. That setting is the usual first suspect; here it was measured not to be the cause.
DisableLastAccess=2 ('System Managed') makes last-access behaviour depend on the machine and its conditions, which is why fixtures back-date and assert a precondition before judging the scan.
Classify a red test as environment drift or a defect before fixing it, and record the alternatives that were rejected.
Mock file systems do not keep directory LastAccessTime, which supports keeping last-access tests on real NTFS trees.
Test frameworks root temporary fixtures in a per-user base folder they choose themselves, not straight in an inherited shared temp folder.
CI agents and services running as LocalSystem inherit TEMP=C:\Windows\Temp, a well-known source of tests that fail only on build machines.

prior_art.where: Mark Russinovich, UAC internals article (quoted by the investigation, not in this run's search block)

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Test tooling on shared or service machines (pytest's per-user tmp base, CI agents running as LocalSystem)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Do not trust an inherited TEMP for fixtures: root them in a per-user base you choose. Keep one deliberate test in the hostile location so its behaviour stays visible and does not get filed as known noise.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The project's failure is exactly the CI-agent one: the engine's shell inherits the machine TEMP. The usual cure, a per-user base, would on its own hide a real product effect that exists only in that location. So the transfer is taken only paired with explicit Facts in that location, protected by architecture rule 1.

taste_disagreements: Whether 'Counting-rule tests build real NTFS trees in %TEMP%' is honoured by %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when the process TEMP is the machine's. This design reads it as the user's own TEMP (the HKCU value, measured). A stricter reader may disagree.
kept == unmoved (chosen; also catches under-counting, and trips if luafv stops acting) vs kept <= unmoved (the bug test's weaker form, which would not trip on a machine without luafv).
Whether default-suite Facts should write into C:\Windows\Temp at all, a folder this user cannot list, so a failed cleanup there is unrecoverable without an administrator.
Whether the counter correction deserves a KnownWorkarounds checkbox. This design says no: it changes no scan behaviour and corrects this project's own false count.
Parent identity in the correction: path text in a per-scan set (chosen) vs a per-folder flag or index carried by the walk (no path handling, but it changes the walk's work items).
